title: Host for Free, Then Pay with Limits
subtitle: How free hosting gets your project live in minutes
intro: You built a project. Now you want the world to see it without paying for a server first.
takeaway: Free hosting trades money for limits, so pick the right home for your project type before you deploy.

sections.heading: Analogy: free hosting is like a free food court stall
sections.body:
Imagine a food court gives you a tiny stall for free to test your recipe. You get a table, power, and customers walking by.

Free hosting is the same. A hosting platform is a computer on the internet that shows your site to others. A free tier is a small free slice of that computer.

You push your code with Git-based deployment, which means every git push can auto-publish your site. That leads to why this exists.

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: show work fast without servers
sections.body:
Developers need to deploy, which means putting your code live on a public URL, without buying servers.

For a static site, which is just HTML, CSS and images with no server code, use Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, or Surge. For a backend or full app, use Fly.io with global edge deployment, which runs your code close to users, or Google Cloud free tier.

This is perfect for portfolios and demos. But free is not infinite, which is what breaks next.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: the free stall gets crowded
sections.body:
Free tiers have hard limits to prevent abuse.

- Sleep: Heroku-style free apps turn off when idle and wake slowly
- Caps: bandwidth, build minutes, or hours per month run out
- No guarantees: no uptime promise and your site can be removed

If 10,000 people visit at once, your free Fly.io or Netlify site may throttle, sleep, or show an error page. Start free to learn, then plan to upgrade when real users arrive.

steps.narration: You have a project on your laptop and GitHub.
You push, and the host auto-builds it.
Free host publishes it to a public URL.
Edge servers copy it close to users for speed.
Too much traffic hits the free cap and slows or sleeps.

options: Putting your code live on a public URL
quiz.why: Deploy means publishing your project so others can visit it via a hosting platform.

quiz.q: Which free host fits which project?
options: Fly.io for static HTML only, Netlify for databases
Netlify/Cloudflare Pages for static sites, Fly.io/Google Cloud for backends
quiz.why: Static site hosts serve files; Fly.io and Google Cloud run server code and edge apps.

quiz.q: What breaks first if usage grows 100x on a free tier?
options: You hit caps: sleep, bandwidth limits, or throttling
quiz.why: Free tiers limit hours, bandwidth and builds, so spikes cause sleep or errors before you upgrade.

extra: Free tiers often require adding a credit card for verification even if cost is $0.
